solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, mirror symmetry); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crooked city alarms me when rebuilt

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A twisted cityscape: the alarms of a city going off as it is reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when rebuilt' tells you to rearrange CITY ALARMS ME, all twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crooked is lopsided, lacking balance between its two sides.

clue.text: A cold fish accepting she shows weakness

parts.note: a chill is a coldness

indicators.note: a thing accepting another takes it inside, so the fish holds the word she

parts.note: an eel is a fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cold, fishy person who takes someone in reveals a vulnerability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' signals the insertion; 'cold' is an adjective in the surface but gives a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles was vulnerable only at his heel, so the phrase names a single fatal flaw.

clue.text: Unusually frosty north: undergarment found

indicators.note: doing something unusually means not in the normal way, so these letters come out in a new order

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: In a strangely cold northern place, a pair of underpants turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges FROSTY plus N. Y-fronts are British men's briefs whose front seams form an upside-down Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are a style of men's briefs, worn under clothing.

clue.text: Runs to escape bad-tempered elk

indicators.note: the runs escaping means that letter gets out of the word and is lost

parts.note: morose means sullen and bad-tempered
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An irritable elk charges off to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to escape' takes R out of MOROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the European elk is the same animal North Americans call a moose.

clue.text: European in marquee establishes principle

indicators.note: the European being in the marquee means that letter goes inside the tent

parts.note: a marquee is a large tent

explanation.surface: A European in a big tent lays down a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine held as true, such as a guiding rule.

clue.text: Pub brings in satellite after opening? It's born of necessity!

indicators.note: the pub bringing things in means they go inside its letters

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: the satellite comes after the opening, so it follows in the answer

parts.note: a vent is an opening
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A pub somehow takes in a satellite on its opening day, which must be necessity's offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: Io is one of Jupiter's moons, a crossword staple. The definition plays on the saying 'necessity is the mother of invention'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb calls necessity the mother of invention, so an invention is its child.

clue.text: Pair connected somehow more than usually liable to mishap

definitions.text: more than usually liable to mishap

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so these letters are arranged in a new way

explanation.surface: Two people linked together in some way are especially prone to mishaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal sits between fodder and definition; all thirteen letters of PAIR CONNECTED are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps having accidents is described as prone to them.

clue.text: Appropriate to support Her Majesty

parts.note: to prop is to support
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: It is fitting to back the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper and appropriate are synonyms meaning suitable or correct.

clue.text: Talk tediously about old whale killer

indicators.note: talk going about something surrounds it, so the phrase wraps around the letter

parts.note: to harp on is to talk tediously about one subject

explanation.surface: Someone drones on about an old whale hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion splits the phrasal verb between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpoon is the barbed spear thrown or fired to kill whales.

clue.text: Clergyman bringing six to vehicle

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A clergyman drives a carload of six people.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a Church of England parish priest.

clue.text: Butcher's no good for pop

indicators.note: no good means without the good, so its letter is removed

parts.note: butcher's is short for butcher's hook, Cockney rhyming slang for look, so a glance

explanation.surface: A butcher who is useless with a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look. 'no' drops G from GLANCE. 'pop' is a verb here: to pierce a boil.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance a boil is to pierce it, much as you would pop a blister.

clue.text: Top nude worked out, firm through exercise

indicators.note: letters worked out are processed into a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A naked top model has been to the gym and is now firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges TOP NUDE and also echoes the gym theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscles toned up by exercise are firmer and better defined.

clue.text: One as eligible keeps artistic support?

indicators.note: the phrase keeps the answer within its words, spanning their letters

explanation.surface: Someone who is eligible holds on to a support for the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the stand that holds a painter's canvas.

clue.text: Involved in a cult that's crazy

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Getting caught up in a cult is madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' looks like it goes with 'in', but it rearranges IN A CULT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunatic as an adjective means mad or wildly foolish.

clue.text: Top criminal seizing power

indicators.note: the criminal seizing power grabs it and holds it inside

parts.note: a sinner is a wrongdoer, here a criminal
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A leading criminal takes control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective meaning chief, but it is the spinning toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning top is a toy that spins, so a spinner is one.

clue.text: South African right to eat fish

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A South African says it is the right moment to tuck into some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardine is a small oily sea fish often sold tinned.

clue.text: Hard nut in bad accident

indicators.note: bad means faulty or damaged, so these letters are put in a broken order

explanation.surface: A tough guy is involved in a nasty crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit-and-run is a road collision where the driver leaves without stopping.

clue.text: Written in Sanskrit, he takes letter to Greeks

indicators.note: the answer is written inside these words, running across their letters

explanation.surface: A man writing in Sanskrit carries a letter to the Greeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Old man died in flat

parts.note: old man is slang for father, so pa

explanation.surface: An elderly man died in his apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: a place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad is informal slang for one's home, often a flat or apartment.

clue.text: Villain needs second to enter study

indicators.note: the second going to enter the study is put inside it

parts.note: a den is a private study
a mo is a moment or second

explanation.surface: A bad guy needs a moment to come into the study.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, short for moment, is a common crossword stand-in for a second.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil spirit, and loosely any wicked person.

clue.text: To term clerics eccentric creates great disturbance

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Calling the clergy eccentric causes an uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges TO TERM CLERICS, all thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A thunderstorm with lightning is a violent atmospheric disturbance.

clue.text: Endlessly long story is flop

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a saga is a long story

explanation.surface: A novel that goes on forever is a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' trims the last A from SAGA.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to droop or sink, much as something limp flops down.

clue.text: Left in Paris? That's awkward!

explanation.surface: Abandoned in Paris, someone feels embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: The English word gauche, from French for left, means tactless or lacking social grace.

clue.text: Inexperienced eco-politician

definitions.meaning: a member of an environmentalist political party

explanation.surface: A new environmental politician is still learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means naive or untrained, and also names a member of an environmentalist party.
